summary:
Attempt 6 (bab35f3) builds design 10's narrowed slice, and the product code (src) is right. ContainerLayerStore.Resolve is the only reader of the 'wcifs-layer-store' switch. It turns only Exclude into None, so Refuse stays unconditional as F1 decided. KnownWorkarounds, SettingsWindow with ConfirmTurnOffWindow, the notices, and the report's workarounds and core.notScanned fields are all wired end to end, with no half-wired members.

What I ran:
- ContainerLayerStoreTests: 32/32 passed.
- Full Core suite: 532 passed. The 3 failures are the known pre-existing LastAccess/HeldOpenTree ones (DisableLastAccess=2).
- SL-095 repro on this PC's live store: 1 passed.
- PoolWatchCases C-052 (-Protocol -Rehearse end to end): RUN COMPLETE, scratch deleted. C-053 to C-056 also passed.
- WindowCases X-005: answering No, answering Yes and the next launch all passed.
- Fitness: all 81 rules hold.

Every case-matrix test feeds its shape. Every departure from design 10 that matters is declared in the builder's deviations.

Three minor findings, all in the person-run PoolWatch harness and the rule texts:
- The fltmc paste is read from one place and at one time, not where the header says. I reproduced it: a valid list pasted after -Prepare still reports FILTERS UNDECIDED.
- No case feeds any fltmc paste, now that PoolWatchReportTests (O-078's pins) is deleted.
- Three SL-095 rule because-texts still describe ScanArm and a tolerance verdict that this diff deleted or handed to SC-128.

Not run:
- X-001, X-002 and X-006: they need this PC's real store. I checked them by reading.
- The rules harness for S30–S38: it needs --engine-root. I checked each plant by hand against its regex.

Second round: Second round, an adversarial pass over the parsers, boundaries and error paths in this diff. It found two new error paths, both in PoolWatch.ps1's handling of an interrupted session; nothing new in src.

1. **A damaged log line crashes -Report.** One torn or NUL-filled line in marks.jsonl or arms.jsonl makes -Report throw: exit 1, and neither RUN COMPLETE nor RUN INCOMPLETE is printed. I reproduced this with a fixture. A pool-exhaustion session that ends in a crash or a kill leaves exactly that shape.
2. **An interrupted arm leaves the app running unguarded.** Ctrl+C, or a terminating CIM error while an exe arm runs, ends -Protocol with FsAnalyser.exe still scanning and no guard polling. -Report then says that arm 'never started'.

Checked and sound:
- Windows PowerShell 5.1, which the person is told to use for -Protocol:
  - PoolWatch.ps1 parses with 0 errors.
  - `-Protocol -Rehearse` runs end to end: RUN COMPLETE, scratch deleted, exit 0. That needed a writable TEMP, which the person's own TEMP is.
- fltmc paste shapes (UTF-16 and UTF-8 BOMs, the leading blank line, a refusal mixed into a list) are handled by ReadAllLines and Test-FltmcList.
- In Get-Missing, `break` inside the type switch only leaves the switch, as intended.
- The settings hook's answer parsing and the re-tick on 'No' behave as built (X-005 passed in round one).

findings.claim:
The fltmc paste is read in only one place, and only once. The script's own header tells the person to paste somewhere else.
- The header asks for `<RunDir>\fltmc.txt (or the prepare folder's)`. Nothing reads `<RunDir>\fltmc.txt`.
- `<RunDir>\prepare\fltmc.txt` is read only while -Prepare runs, inside Get-EnvironmentRecord.
- -Report never looks at either file. It prints the value frozen into prepare.json.

A person who pastes after -Prepare, which is the natural moment and what the header implies, gets 'FILTERS UNDECIDED' in criterion 3's environment record. The only way to get the list recorded is to run -Prepare again. That republishes the app and overwrites prepare.json's Rpre mark.

I reproduced it. With a valid 'Filter Name  Num Instances' list in both `<RunDir>\fltmc.txt` and `<RunDir>\prepare\fltmc.txt`, written after prepare.json, -Report printed 'FILTERS UNDECIDED: hello', which is the recorded value.
findings.evidence:
- tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:21-23 (the header: 'paste what it prints into <RunDir>\fltmc.txt (or the prepare folder's)').
- :272-278 Get-EnvironmentRecord reads `Join-Path $pasteDir 'fltmc.txt'`. Its only caller is Invoke-Prepare at :513, with `$prepDir`.
- :491-497 Write-RunReport reads only `prepare\prepare.json` `.environment.fltmcFilters`.
- :555 -Prepare's closing message says nothing about pasting.
- docs/design/SL-095-container-layer-store.md:145-147 ('pastes it into fltmc.txt in the prepare folder', with no timing).
findings.fix:
In Write-RunReport, check `<RunDir>\fltmc.txt`, then `<RunDir>\prepare\fltmc.txt`. If either exists, run it through Read-Lines and Test-FltmcList and prefer it over prepare.json's value, naming that file in the FILTERS line.

The smaller alternative is to correct the header (:22) and -Prepare's message (:555) to say 'paste into <RunDir>\prepare\fltmc.txt before running -Prepare'.

findings.claim:
No case feeds an fltmc paste, so Test-FltmcList's branches have no test.

O-078's fix (an fltmc error was counted as recorded) was pinned by xUnit tests in PoolWatchReportTests.cs, and this diff deletes that file. The check is now reimplemented in PowerShell, Test-FltmcList. Every PoolWatchCases fixture and the rehearsal feed only the 'not supplied' shape.

I fed three shapes by hand and all behave correctly today:
- a header-plus-rows list prints 'FILTERS recorded';
- 'Failed to get filter information: 0x80070005' / 'Access is denied.' prints 'FILTERS UNDECIDED';
- other text prints 'FILTERS UNDECIDED'.

Nothing would catch a regression of the O-078 shape. This branch is not on the case matrix.
findings.evidence:
- tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:257-262 (Test-FltmcList: `isList = $header -and -not $refused`).
- :495-496 (the FILTERS line).
- tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1:100: every fixture writes `fltmcFilters = 'not supplied (fixture)'`.
- tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/PoolWatchReportTests.cs: deleted, -551 lines.
findings.fix:
Add two fixture variants to PoolWatchCases, for example inside C-053's clean-run builder:
- prepare.json fltmcFilters set to a 'Filter Name  Num Instances' header plus one row; assert the line 'FILTERS recorded'.
- the same with 'Failed to get filter information: 0x80070005'; assert 'FILTERS UNDECIDED' and no 'FILTERS recorded'.

findings.claim:
Three because-texts of SL-095's own architecture rules describe behaviour that this diff deleted or handed to SC-128:
- 'the measurement rigs never relocate the store' says 'ScanArm has InternalsVisibleTo into Core' and 'voids the protocol's WC* clause'. ScanArm and its InternalsVisibleTo line are deleted here, and the WC* clause is SC-128's.
- 'every directory open goes through the guarded call in DirectoryReader' says 'the tolerance verdict judged by it'. This slice judges no tolerance.
- 'product code never switches the per-file metadata probe off' says the listing-only arm 'lives in tests/window/ScanArm'. That folder is gone.

Every later reviewer reads these texts as the reason the rule exists.
findings.evidence:
- .taad/fitness.yaml:984-987, :994-998 and :1018-1021.
- The deletions: src/FsAnalyser.Core/FsAnalyser.Core.csproj (-3, InternalsVisibleTo ScanArm), tests/window/ScanArm/Program.cs and ScanArm.csproj.
- docs/design/SL-095-container-layer-store.md:189-199 hands the verdicts to SC-128 and records ScanArm as deleted.
findings.fix:
Rewrite the three because-texts in the present tense:
- :1018: no rig has InternalsVisibleTo now. The rule keeps any future rig or the hook from setting the override, which would walk the live layer on the person's fresh boot.
- :987: the counter is what PoolWatch -Report's completeness check and the window report read.
- :996: the listing-only arm was deleted with ScanArm.

findings.evidence:
- tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:382: `Read-Jsonl ... ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertFrom-Json }`, with no per-line guard.
- :40 sets `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`.
- :464-465 Write-RunReport reads both files through Read-Jsonl before anything is printed.
- :551 is the exit 0/2 contract.
findings.fix: In Read-Jsonl, parse each line inside try/catch, and drop NULs with `$_.Trim([char]0, ' ', "`t")` before parsing. Return the parsed objects together with the numbers of lines that failed. In Write-RunReport, add `marks.jsonl line N is not JSON (a torn or unflushed write)` to $missing for each one, so the run reads RUN INCOMPLETE with exit 2 and still prints every net it can.

findings.evidence:
- tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:342-357: Start-Exe, then the `while (-not $p.WaitForExit(2000))` loop calling Get-Pool (:347) and Write-Mark (:356), with no try/finally.
- :617 `try { Invoke-Protocol 'C:\' $stops } finally { SetThreadExecutionState(...) }` resets only the sleep state.
- :397 `$missing.Add("arm ${name}: in the plan but not in arms.jsonl, so it never started")` does not look at $byLabel.

drift: Design 10's component 'NotScanned kind and row' adds a NotScanned EntryKind in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/EntryKind.cs. The build keeps EntryKind.Folder plus an EntryFlags.NotScanned flag, inherited from earlier attempts (EntryKind.cs:6-10). Deviation 1 covers this only by its blanket 'adapted under other names'; it does not name it. The behaviour is equivalent.

Design 10's 'Report writer' component says eng/read-window.ps1 reads the new fields. read-window -Outcome (:184-185) prints skippedStores, opensUnderExcludedStore, outcome and refusal, but neither workarounds nor notScanned. Deviation 9 explains notScanned through skippedStores; workarounds is not mentioned.
